newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 20 pct grain duty likely to return June 30.
newsitem.headline: Polish 20 pct grain duty likely to return June 30.

text.p: Poland is likely to revive its 20 percent grain import duty as planned on June 30 to protect the interests of domestic farmers, a cabinet official said on Monday.

Marek Wagner, secretary of state in the prime minister's office, told reporters he expected at least 1.3 million tonnes of grain to be in warehouses just before this year's harvest in August and September, which meant that there was room to reinstate the full 20 percent import levy and protect producers.

Last year Poland removed the 20 percent levy up to the middle of 1997 to tackle inflation and fast-growing food prices. Earlier this year it reimposed a 10 percent duty on most grains amid pressure from farmers. --Marcin Grajewski +48 22 653 9700
